grader.scenario: Port forwarding and CGNAT issue preventing home Synology NAS server and CCTV from being accessed remotely
grader.notes: Clean 100.0 PASS call demonstrating a brisk, concise, deeply technical agent style (R PASS hard case), a 90s managed hold ([03:34]-[05:28]) plus a 28s router-reboot transition strictly <=30s ([06:11]-[07:01], H PASS hard case), and sharp active listening comparing WAN IP prefixes 100.64.x.x vs 82.14.x.x (AL PASS hard case).

items.name: Branding and Survey Check
items.evidence: [00:00] Agent: 'Good afternoon, thank you for calling S-Net technical support.' / [13:29] Agent: 'Thank you for choosing S-Net, Youssef. Have a great afternoon. Goodbye.'

items.name: Hold time and Dead Air
items.evidence: [03:34] Agent announces a 90s hold ('Please bear with me while I move your subscriber profile off the CGNAT pool onto a public dynamic IPv4') and returns at [05:28] ('Thank you for holding, Youssef.'), plus a 28s router-reboot transition at [06:11]-[07:01] (<=30s threshold).

items.name: Verified customer
items.evidence: [00:22] Agent: 'Let's verify your account first: please confirm your postal address and four-digit security PIN.'

items.name: Personalized the call/ticket appropriately
items.evidence: [00:22] Agent: 'I am sorry for the disruption to your remote access since Tuesday's maintenance, Youssef...'

items.name: Empathy & Acknowledgment Statement
items.evidence: [00:22] Agent: 'I am sorry for the disruption to your remote access since Tuesday's maintenance, Youssef—I understand how frustrating it is when working port forwards suddenly stop responding.'

items.name: Paraphrasing
items.evidence: [00:43] Agent: 'To summarize the issue in my own words: since Tuesday's maintenance, external connections to your Synology NAS and Hikvision CCTV over your Hub 4 port forwarding rules are failing, even though your home fibre is online.'

items.name: Active listening
items.evidence: [01:47]-[02:24] Agent compares the Hub 4 WAN IP (100.64.118.42) against external IP (185.94.212.19), and at [07:19]-[07:57] verifies the new 82.14.209.73 public IP and exact ports (TCP 5001 to 192.168.1.50 and TCP 8000 to 192.168.1.60).

items.name: Took ownership of the problem
items.evidence: [03:18] Agent: 'I will move your subscriber profile onto our dynamic public IPv4 pool free of charge.' / [09:57] Agent permanently sets 'CGNAT-Exempt=TRUE' on the circuit.

items.name: Build rapport and observed professionalism
items.evidence: [02:24], [07:39], [11:55] Agent maintains a brisk, concise, deeply technical, and highly professional style without unnecessary small talk, which the customer praises at [11:55].

items.name: Probing
items.evidence: [01:12]-[02:07] Agent systematically probes the forwarded TCP/UDP ports, manual vs UPnP rules, Hub 4 WAN IPv4 prefix, and external ifconfig.me IP.

items.name: Confirmed the issue is resolved
items.evidence: [09:19] & [09:47] Customer tests both TCP 5001 (Synology DSM) and TCP 8000 (Hikvision CCTV) over 5G and confirms at [13:23]: 'No, both remote services are 100% resolved and working properly'.
